enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **a)** Tell a story that ends with, "... I wish I had listened to the advice of my teachers and parents."
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: a hard-working pupil from a poor family, supported by parents and teachers.
2. Rising action: bad company and laziness, lies to the parents, warnings ignored.
3. Climax: poor test marks, the father's silent disappointment, failure in the examination.
4. Resolution: the mother's forgiveness and the decision to repeat the class.
5. Ending: the required closing sentence.

**Model composition (483 words)**

It was the beginning of my final year in Form Five, and I was the happiest girl in our compound. My parents were poor farmers, yet they had sold part of their cocoa harvest every term to pay my school fees. Each evening my mother would say, "Read your books before you sleep," and my father would add, "Education is the only inheritance we can give you." My teachers, too, never tired of warning us that the General Certificate of Education examination rewards only those who prepare early. I nodded politely, but I did not take any of it seriously.

Soon I made new friends who spent their evenings at a video club near the market. At first I went there only on Fridays. Then it became Wednesdays as well, and later almost every day. I told my mother that I was attending extra lessons, and she believed me because she trusted me. In class I slept at my desk, and my homework was copied hurriedly from a classmate's book. When Mr. Fomba, my English teacher, called me aside and asked what was troubling me, I laughed and said that I was simply tired.

The first test of the term came, and I scored eight out of twenty in mathematics. I tore the paper into small pieces and threw it away so that no one at home would see it. At the end of the second term, the principal sent a letter to my parents. My father read it slowly under the lantern, and I saw tears in his eyes for the first time. He did not shout. He only said, "We have given you everything we have." His quiet voice hurt me more than any beating could have done. I promised to change, but the promise lasted only one week.

By the time the examination timetable was pinned on the notice board, I realised that I had hardly covered half of the syllabus. I tried to read all night, but the words were like strangers to me. In the examination hall my hands trembled, and I left several questions blank. When the results were published three months later, I had passed only two subjects. My friends from the video club had disappeared, and not one of them came to console me.

I sat behind our house, ashamed to face my mother. She came and sat beside me, held my hand and said gently, "There is always another chance, my child." I wept bitterly. I thought of Mr. Fomba's warnings, my father's sacrifices and the many evenings I had wasted. Today I am repeating Form Five in a different school, and I study with determination. But whenever I meet my former classmates, who are now in Lower Sixth, a deep pain fills my heart, and I whisper to myself, "... I wish I had listened to the advice of my teachers and parents."

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. A story that does not end with the exact sentence given in the topic.
2. Telling the story as a list of events with no build-up, dialogue or feeling, and mixing past and present tenses.
